title: notify: a written-out email address no user holds, on a node that does not name the email channel, writes an inbox row nobody can read and the node reports success
body:
Filing gate **③, a finding a contract review escalated**: the `## Contract review` of PR #25739 (`6395784809`, card #25696, flag F2) raised it as an authoring trap needing a carrier. Filed by `domain:spec` seat 2 (seat post #18549) · `sunhaolin` · session `session_01PC4NPXPgPmpDRG9DdDnyXT`. ⛔ Not a claim. Grade and domain are triage's. The seat suggests `domain:server` (messaging), and `domain:spec` if the fix is an authoring rule.

## The trap (measured on `main` `5874d25302`)

Ruling B on #25647 (`6386629237`) makes an address written out in `recipients` an **author constant**, "sent as written". On a node whose `channels` include `email`, that holds: `RecipientResolver.resolveOne` → `resolveEmail` maps the address to the user who holds it, or keeps it verbatim on a miss, and the email channel mails a verbatim address (`email-channel.ts` `EMAIL_SHAPE(recipient)` branch).

On a node that does **not** name `email`, a verbatim address goes to the inbox channel, which is the messaging default when `channels` is absent:

- `packages/services/service-messaging/src/inbox-channel.ts:149` reads `const userId = delivery.recipient;`, and `:205` writes the row with `user_id: userId`. There is no check that the value is a user id.
- So `recipients: 'exec@example.com'` with no user holding that address writes a `sys_inbox_message` row whose `user_id` is the address string. No user's inbox query matches it. The delivery is recorded and the node reports success.

**Live instance:** `examples/app-showcase/src/automation/flows/index.ts` node `alert_exec` (around `:1435`): `recipients: 'exec@example.com'`, no `channels`, so inbox only. The "Alert Exec" branch of that flow notifies nobody.

The #25696 describe text (PR #25739) claims nothing for this case, so it is not false. It is a silent no-op that an author, or an AI writing a flow, will not notice.

## Fix directions (not chosen here)

- **A. Refuse at authoring.** A `notify` node whose `recipients` writes out an email-shaped string, and whose `channels` do not include `email`, is refused at `os validate` / publish, with a message pointing to `channels: 'email'` or to a user id. This is loud and contract-first. It is a narrowing, so the in-repo producer above changes.
- **B. Refuse at delivery.** The inbox channel refuses, or dead-letters, a recipient that is not a user id. This is loud at run time, but only after a run.
- **C. Do both.**

## Dedupe

Searched `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack notify recipient written-out email address inbox only channel no user`: no open card covers it. #17611 (email delivery with no transport, closed) is a different path. **New.**
